sources.title: Atherosclerosis: A Problem in Newer Public Health

provenance.author: Ancel Keys
provenance.venue: Journal of the Mount Sinai Hospital

sources.notes: Early influential paper arguing for a diet-heart link. Keys's later Seven Countries Study was more influential; this earlier paper established the framework. Methodological criticisms of Keys's country selection have been raised in subsequent decades.

sources.title: Egg consumption and risk of coronary heart disease and stroke: dose-response meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies

author: Ying Rong
Li Chen
Tingting Zhu
Yadong Song
Meng Yu
Zhilei Shan
An Pan
Frank B. Hu
Liegang Liu
provenance.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology / Harvard School of Public Health

sources.notes: Meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies. Found no significant association between egg consumption and coronary heart disease or stroke risk in the general population, but found increased risk in diabetic patients.

sources.title: Association of Egg Consumption with Cardiovascular Disease in a Large Cohort of US Adults
sources.notes: Large prospective cohort study. Found that each additional half egg per day was significantly associated with higher risk of cardiovascular disease and all-cause mortality. Contradicts the 2013 Rong meta-analysis in direction. Sparked renewed debate.

sources.title: 2015-2020 Dietary Guidelines for Americans

provenance.author: Dietary Guidelines Advisory Committee
provenance.institution: US Department of Health and Human Services / US Department of Agriculture

sources.conflict_of_interest: The 2015 DGAC process has been criticized for food industry involvement in past cycles. This conflict is documented in academic literature.
sources.notes: Removed the longstanding 300mg/day dietary cholesterol limit. Stated that 'cholesterol is not a nutrient of concern for overconsumption.' This represented a significant shift from prior guidance.

sources.title: Dietary cholesterol and cardiovascular disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.conflict_of_interest: Fernandez has received research funding from the egg industry (American Egg Board / Egg Nutrition Center). This is a documented conflict relevant to interpreting her work on eggs.
sources.notes: Review arguing that dietary cholesterol does not significantly affect cardiovascular risk in most individuals. Conflict of interest is relevant here.

sources.title: Industry funding and the nutritional research agenda: A systematic review of systematic reviews

author: Maira Bes-Rastrollo
Matthias B. Schulze
Miguel Ruiz-Canela
Miguel A. Martinez-Gonzalez
provenance.institution: University of Navarra / German Institute of Human Nutrition

sources.notes: Meta-level study documenting the relationship between industry funding and favorable nutrition research conclusions. Provides the evidential basis for weighting industry-funded studies in this dispute.
